Utah model chill units

Source: R/chill_units.R
chill_units.Rd

Accumulates chill units (CU) with the Utah model of Richardson, Seeley & Walker (1974). Each hourly temperature receives a weight that can be positive, zero or negative; the accumulation is the running sum of weights.

Usage

chill_units(
  temperature,
  method = "utah",
  output = c("cumulative", "hourly", "total"),
  na_action = c("propagate", "skip")
)

Arguments

temperature

Numeric vector, or matrix with one row per series and one column per hour, of hourly temperatures in degrees Celsius.

method

Currently only "utah".

output

"cumulative" (default) running sum, "hourly" weights or "total" sum.

na_action

"propagate" (default): the running sum becomes NA from the first missing hour; "skip": missing hours contribute zero and their count is returned in the "n_missing" attribute.

Value

Chill units (dimensionless) with the shape implied by output.

Weights and boundary convention

The original model is stated in tenths of a degree Celsius. For continuous temperatures thermify uses left-open, right-closed intervals \((a, b]\), the same convention as chillR::Utah_Model():

Temperature (degrees C)Weight
\(T \le 1.4\)0
\(1.4 < T \le 2.4\)0.5
\(2.4 < T \le 9.1\)1
\(9.1 < T \le 12.4\)0.5
\(12.4 < T \le 15.9\)0
\(15.9 < T \le 18.0\)-0.5
\(T > 18.0\)-1

Negative weights are kept and the running sum is not truncated at zero. Variants that reset or floor the sum (for example the "positive Utah" model) are different models and are not applied implicitly.

Input

temperature must be an hourly series, observed or reconstructed with hourly_temperatures(), ordered in time with one value per hour. Applying the weights to monthly or daily means is not meaningful because the weight function is non-linear and non-monotonic.

References

Richardson, E. A., Seeley, S. D., & Walker, D. R. (1974). A model for estimating the completion of rest for 'Redhaven' and 'Elberta' peach trees. HortScience, 9(4), 331-332.

See also

utah_weights(), chill_portions().

Examples

temp <- c(0, 2, 5, 10, 14, 17, 20)
utah_weights(temp)
#> [1]  0.0  0.5  1.0  0.5  0.0 -0.5 -1.0
chill_units(temp)
#> [1] 0.0 0.5 1.5 2.0 2.0 1.5 0.5
chill_units(temp, output = "total")
#> [1] 0.5
